chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Marriage is not permissible today in Islam by way of employment (ijarah), that is, if one says: 'I will work for you for such and such a year on the condition that you marry me to your sister or your daughter.' He (peace be upon him) said: It is forbidden, because it is the price of her neck (body), and she is more entitled to her dowry.

key_terms.رَقَبَة: Neck, metaphorically referring to the person/body

ai.seo_question: Is marriage valid if it is exchanged for employment services?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the chapter on dowries, highlighting the Shia juristic view that 'marriage for service' (nikah al-ijarah) is invalid because the labor serves as a price for the woman's personhood, potentially depriving her of her independent right to the full dowry. This reflects the principle that mahr is a direct right of the wife, distinct from any contractual consideration for her hand in marriage.
